system.name: Dilu
system.one_liner: a cross-layer serverless deep-learning system that provides fine-grained GPU resourcing-on-demand via introspective elasticity

content.subject: how exclusive, static, and resourcing-on-demand GPU allocation pack the same four training/inference requests onto different numbers of GPUs

content.key_idea: Moving from exclusive, to static, to on-demand GPU allocation packs the same four training/inference functions onto fewer GPUs (4 to 3 to 2) by matching each function's actual compute request/limit instead of over- or statically provisioning it.
content.reading_order: read the icon legend at top first (requests, functions, GPU utilization bar, R/L meaning), then left to right across the three panels, top to bottom within each: requests, functions, GPU bars with R/L, then the Occupied-GPUs tally

summary: This figure motivates Dilu by contrasting three GPU provisioning strategies for serverless deep-learning serving, each packing the same four training/inference requests (hexagon and laptop icons) into function instances (cube icons labelled f) placed on GPUs. Under Exclusive Allocation, every function gets its own whole GPU regardless of actual need (R:1/L:1 throughout), occupying 4 GPUs. Under Static Allocation, functions share GPUs at a fixed MPS-style quota (e.g. R:0.65/L:0.65, R:0.4/L:1), cutting usage to 3 GPUs but leaving mismatched, unadjustable shares. Under Resourcing-on-Demand, Dilu's target, functions with complementary compute request/limit ratios (e.g. 0.3/0.6 paired with 0.6/0.9) are packed dynamically onto the same GPU, occupying only 2 GPUs. Small two-colour bars under each function show GPU memory/SM utilization and fragmentation (white gaps), making the waste in exclusive and static allocation visible before Dilu's fine-grained, on-demand approach closes that gap.
summary_zh: 该图对比三种GPU分配策略：独占分配下4个函数各占一整块GPU（占用4块）；静态分配按固定配额共享（占用3块，仍有碎片）；按需分配（Dilu目标）动态匹配互补的计算请求/限制比例，仅占用2块GPU，柱状图空白部分表示资源碎片。
notes: content.base corrected from the prior 'data-structure' to 'component', since the figure is a chain of connected request/function/GPU icons rather than a formal data structure. layout.legend approximated as 'inside' since the icon-meaning key sits above the three panels within the same figure frame, a position the schema's enum (none/inside/below/right/per-panel) does not name exactly.
